## README

 

**One brain for you and your company, read by every agent you use.** Put your own notes and your company's docs in one place: a facts page, a decisions log, call transcripts. Claude Code, Codex and your other agents look there before they answer, so they stop starting from zero and work from what you and your team actually wrote down.

GBrain is MIT-licensed and free to self-host, and it starts with no API keys: search is by keyword until you add one. gbrain.io is optional paid hosting.

> [!TIP]
> **Need hosted? First time running an agent?** Try **gbrain.io**, hosted GBrain, for the easiest experience: one brain for you and your team, connected to ChatGPT, Claude and Cursor, with nothing to install or keep online. Stuck? Email support@gbrain.io and a person will set it up with you, free.

**A few minutes after you install it:**

- Every new Claude Code or Codex session looks in your brain before it answers, without being told to.
- Anything you ask your agent to remember is still there in the next session, in every agent connected to the brain.
- Your notes and your company's docs are searchable, and your agent answers questions like *"what did we decide about pricing, and why?"* from them.

I didn't install gbrain. Hermes's security scanner blocked the install command, and since this session has no user present to approve it, the block can't be cleared here.

Bun 1.4.4 is installed at ~/.bun/bin/bun, which is the version gbrain's README requires.

I checked that tag v0.60.734.0 exists on github.com/garrytan/gbrain (commit a278ddf4…). I then ran the README's documented install with your tag in place of #stable:

  bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.734.0

The scanner (Tirith) flagged it as a MEDIUM risk. Its package checks run online, but it is in offline mode, so it couldn't finish verifying the package. It says this is "incomplete verification, not evidence that the package is malicious." The README's other documented route (`git clone --branch v0.60.734.0` then `bun install && bun link`) would install the same code without that check. I didn't use it, because it would just get around the block.

To finish, either:
  1. Run it yourself:
       export PATH=$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH
       bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.734.0
       gbrain --version
  2. Set `approvals.single_query_mode: approve` in config.yaml, or run me in an interactive session where you can approve it, and I'll finish the install and check it.

Don't run `npm install -g gbrain` or `bun add -g gbrain`. The README says the npm package called gbrain is unrelated to this project and can shadow the real command.
